prerequisites: Having passed the course 'Introduction to Formula Student'
Must be taken in parallel with 'Formula Student II'

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of the degree.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage mandatory specifications, regulations, and standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to organize and plan resources and people within a company, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Adopt a responsible, organized attitude towards work and be willing to learn, considering the challenge of continuous training.
Apply the strategies of scientific methodology: analyze the problematic situation qualitatively and quantitatively, propose hypotheses and solutions using engineering models.
Work effectively in a group, integrating capabilities and knowledge to make decisions in the field of professional practice linked to the degree.

syllabus_topics: Specific training for the design and manufacturing of single-seater systems/subsystems.
Study of alternatives and feasibility for a system/subsystem of a competition single-seater.
Design of a system/subsystem of a competition single-seater.
Manufacturing of the system/subsystem of a competition single-seater.
Assembly and Validation of the system/subsystem of a competition single-seater.

assessment_methods.method: Individual Project (comprising 4 activities: study of alternatives/feasibility, detailed design, manufacturing, assembly/validation)
Attendance and active participation in project activities

assessment_rules: To pass the course, it is essential to obtain at least 50% from the sum of all evaluation mechanisms. It is not possible to waive continuous assessment due to the nature of the pilot project. It will be assumed that the student waives the evaluation if they do not submit the assigned project. A final evaluation is not contemplated for ordinary or extraordinary sessions; the same evaluation and waiver mechanisms apply.
